last_result.content:
# VitalPath Subscription Agreement

## 1.1 Platform and Services

VitalPath Inc. ("Provider") will make its wellness-engagement platform available to Beacon
Manufacturing Company ("Customer") for use by Customer's eligible employees and their
enrolled dependents. The platform supports activity challenges, coaching, scheduling of
on-site health events, incentive tracking, and reporting to Customer's benefits team.

## 2.1 Fees and Subscription Term

The subscription fee is $300,000 per year for up to 8,500 eligible employees, invoiced
annually in advance. The initial Subscription Term is three years, beginning on the Service
Commencement Date.

## 3.1 Employee Data

"Employee Data" means data about Customer's employees and their enrolled dependents that is
submitted to or generated by the platform, including registration data, program
participation records, device and activity data, coaching notes, and any screening or
assessment results Customer or its designees upload. As between the parties, Customer
retains all right, title, and interest in Employee Data. Customer grants Provider a
nonexclusive, worldwide, royalty-free right to host, process, transmit, and display Employee
Data to operate the platform, together with the additional rights set out in the Data
Handling Exhibit.

## 4.2 Customer Responsibilities

Customer is responsible for obtaining any consents, authorizations, and notices required for
Provider to receive and process Employee Data, and for the accuracy of data Customer
uploads. Provider has no obligation to determine whether Customer has obtained them.

## 5.2 Confidentiality

Each party will protect the other's Confidential Information with at least the care it uses
for its own confidential information of like importance, and in no event less than
reasonable care. Employee Data is Customer's Confidential Information, except as otherwise
provided in the Data Handling Exhibit.

## 7.3 Support and Provider Personnel Access

Provider's support, engineering, and customer-success personnel may access Employee Data,
including identifiable records, from any location and on any device suited to the task, in
order to resolve Customer tickets, tune platform configuration, and perform maintenance and
migration work. Provider will use personnel it considers qualified and will determine in its
discretion which personnel require access. Provider makes no commitment to role-based access
restrictions, device management, session recording, or access logging beyond its internal
practices as they may change from time to time.

## 8.4 Warranty and Disclaimer

Provider warrants that the platform will perform materially in accordance with its then-
current documentation. Except as expressly stated, the platform is provided "as is" and
Provider disclaims all implied warranties.

## 10.3 Limitation of Liability

Except for Customer's payment obligations and each party's confidentiality obligations, each
party's aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement will not exceed the
fees paid by Customer in the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to liability.

## 12.2 Governing Law and Venue

This Agreement is governed by the laws of the State of Illinois, without regard to its
conflicts-of-laws rules. The parties consent to exclusive venue in the state and federal
courts sitting in Cook County, Illinois.

## 13.1 Incorporation and Precedence

The Data Handling Exhibit is incorporated into and forms part of this Agreement. With
respect to its subject matter, the Data Handling Exhibit controls over any conflicting term
of this Agreement.

# VitalPath Data Handling Exhibit

## 1.2 Definitions

"Employee Data" has the meaning given in Section 3.1 of the Agreement. "De-Identified Data"
means Employee Data from which the direct identifiers listed in Section 3.2 have been removed
or replaced in accordance with Provider's de-identification procedure. "Security Incident"
means unauthorized access to, acquisition of, or disclosure of Employee Data in Provider's
possession or control.

## 2.1 Permitted Processing

Provider will process Employee Data to operate, secure, support, and administer the platform
for Customer, to prepare the reports described in the Order Form, and as otherwise permitted
by this Exhibit. Provider will maintain an information-security program consistent with
generally accepted industry practice for platforms of similar type and scale.

## 3.2 De-Identification and Analytics

Provider maintains a documented de-identification procedure under which direct identifiers,
including name, email address, employee identification number, and street address, are
removed from or replaced with a persistent pseudonymous token in a record before that record
is used for any purpose described in this Section 3.2. Provider may create De-Identified Data
from Employee Data and may use, reproduce, distribute, license, and sell De-Identified Data,
alone or combined with data from other customers, for benchmarking, research, product
development, and any other lawful business purpose, including after expiration or termination
of the Agreement. De-Identified Data is Provider's property. Customer acknowledges that
De-Identified Data is not Employee Data and that the remaining provisions of this Exhibit do
not apply to it.

## 4.1 Retention and Post-Termination Handling

Provider will retain Employee Data during the Subscription Term and thereafter for so long as
Provider determines retention is necessary or appropriate for legal, regulatory, audit, or
dispute-resolution purposes. Following expiration or termination, Provider will make Employee
Data available for Customer export for thirty (30) days, after which Provider will delete
Employee Data in accordance with Provider's standard retention schedule then in effect.
Provider has no obligation to certify deletion or to delete Employee Data held in backup,
archival, log, or aggregated form.

## 5.3 Security Incident Notification

Provider will notify Customer of a Security Incident that Provider has confirmed resulted in
unauthorized acquisition of Employee Data and that materially affects Customer. Provider will
give that notice after completing its initial investigation and determining the scope of the
incident. Provider will determine the content, form, and timing of the notice, and may
withhold information that Provider believes could compromise its investigation, its systems
security, or an ongoing law-enforcement inquiry.

## 6.1 Compliance Documentation

Upon written request no more than once per contract year, Provider will make available a
summary of its most recent third-party security assessment. Customer has no right to audit,
inspect, test, or assess Provider's systems, facilities, personnel, or records, and no
obligation of Provider to complete security questionnaires, diligence packets, or similar
assessments is created by this Exhibit or the Agreement.

## 7.2 Subprocessors and Processing Locations

Provider may engage subprocessors to process Employee Data and will publish a current list at
its trust center. Provider will impose on each subprocessor written obligations no less
protective in substance than this Exhibit with respect to Employee Data. Provider and its
subprocessors may process Employee Data in the United States and in any other country in
which Provider or a subprocessor maintains operations.

## 8.3 Return of Materials on Request

Provider will, on Customer's written request during the Subscription Term, export Employee
Data to Customer in Provider's then-standard format at no additional charge, not more than
four times per contract year.

action.title: Concerns with De-Identification and Analytics
action.analysis: The agreement allows VitalPath to create De-Identified Data from Employee Data and use it for various purposes, including selling it. This poses a significant risk to the privacy and confidentiality of Beacon's employees, as the de-identification process may not be sufficient to prevent re-identification.
action.recommendation: We should negotiate stronger protections for Employee Data, including more stringent de-identification standards and restrictions on the use and sale of De-Identified Data.

quotes.text: "Provider may create De-Identified Data from Employee Data and may use, reproduce, distribute, license, and sell De-Identified Data, alone or combined with data from other customers, for benchmarking, research, product development, and any other lawful business purpose, including after expiration or termination of the Agreement."

action.replacement_text: Provider may create De-Identified Data from Employee Data and may use, reproduce, distribute, license, and sell De-Identified Data, alone or combined with data from other customers, for benchmarking, research, product development, and any other lawful business purpose, provided that such use, reproduction, distribution, licensing, and sale is subject to the following conditions: (i) Provider shall ensure that the de-identification process meets the standards set forth in the HIPAA Safe Harbor Methodology or an equivalent standard recognized by the National Institute of Standards and Technology; (ii) Provider shall not sell De-Identified Data to third parties without Customer's prior written consent; and (iii) Provider shall provide Customer with an annual report detailing the use and disposition of De-Identified Data.
action.rationale: This redline strengthens the de-identification standards and imposes restrictions on the use and sale of De-Identified Data, thereby enhancing the protection of Employee Data.
